cards.text: The soldiers are leading Jesus out to crucify Him (Mark 15:20). Right then, a man named Simon of Cyrene is passing by on his way in from the country. He's the father of Alexander and Rufus.

cards.question: The soldiers stop Simon of Cyrene. What do they force him to do?

answers.text: Lead the soldiers to the hill

cards.text: They bring Jesus to a place called Golgotha, which means The Place of the Skull. There they offer Him wine mixed with myrrh.

cards.question: At Golgotha, Jesus drinks the wine mixed with myrrh.

cards.text: “And they crucified Him.” This part is heavy, friend.

cards.question: Then the soldiers divide Jesus' garments by casting lots. What are the lots deciding?

cards.text: It's the third hour when they crucify Him. And there's a charge written against Him, friend, using the same title Pilate kept asking about at the trial (Mark 15:2, 9, 12).

cards.question: What does the charge written against Jesus say?

cards.text: They crucify two robbers with Him, one on His right and one on His left. The charge says King, friend, and look where they put Him.

People passing by shake their heads and heap abuse on Him. They mock Him as the One who's going to destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days, an echo of what the false witnesses said at His trial (Mark 14:57-58).

cards.question: What do the people passing by dare Jesus to do?

answers.text: Come down from the cross and save Himself
Call down fire from heaven on them
Tear down the temple right now

cards.text: The chief priests and scribes join in, mocking Him among themselves: “He saved others, but He cannot save Himself!” Friend, read that line one more time, slowly.

cards.question: Mocking among themselves, the chief priests and scribes say they'll believe if the Christ, the King of Israel, comes down from the cross now.
Even the two robbers crucified with Jesus berate Him.

cards.text: Then comes the sixth hour, right around midday, friend, when the sun should be at its brightest. But something comes over all the land, and it stays until the ninth hour.

cards.question: From the sixth hour until the ninth hour, ___ came over all the land.

cards.text: At the ninth hour, Jesus cries out in a loud voice, “Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?” It means, “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?”

cards.question: Some people standing nearby hear Jesus cry out “Eloi, Eloi…” Who do they think He's calling?

cards.text: Somebody runs over, fills a sponge with sour wine, puts it on a reed and holds it up for Jesus to drink. Now listen close, friend, to what he says while he's holding it up.

cards.question: As he holds up the sponge of sour wine, the man says to leave Jesus alone and see if Elijah comes to take Him down.

cards.text: “But Jesus let out a loud cry and breathed His last.” I think this one hurts, friend.

cards.question: Jesus has breathed His last. Then Mark takes us to the temple, where something is torn in two. What is it?

cards.text: Torn in two from top to bottom, friend. And a Roman centurion standing right in front of Jesus sees how He breathed His last, and he speaks up.

cards.question: The centurion standing in front of Jesus has seen how He breathed His last. When he speaks up, he mocks Jesus like the others did.

cards.text: Here's what the centurion says: “Truly this man was the Son of God!” Out loud, friend, right there in front of Him.

cards.question: The centurion isn't the only one there. Women are watching from a distance too. Who is one of them?
Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome had followed Jesus and ministered to Him before. Where?

cards.text: And many other women had come up to Jerusalem with Him too. We'll stop right here for now, friend, because this story isn't finished.
